_comment: Copy to config.local.json (gitignored) and edit. This overlay is applied on
top of whichever config.<plugin>.json you run, so one copy serves all three.
IMPORTANT — only include keys you actually want to CHANGE. There is no way to
say 'unset' in JSON: an empty string is a value and it OVERWRITES whatever the
plugin config had. Leaving a placeholder like "individual_id": "" here will
blank out config.mock.json's seeded identity and the run will fail in a way
that looks nothing like a config problem. Delete a line rather than empty it.
This is the ONLY config file that should ever hold a credential. The
per-plugin files are tracked; never put a secret in one, even temporarily.
In containers this file is usually absent — compose and Rancher inject the
same values as environment variables, which take precedence over both files.
plans[] is the one array that merges entry by entry rather than replacing:
an overlay listing {"config_file": ...} twice keeps both plans' names from
the plugin file and only swaps their client/jwks paths. Listing FEWER entries
than the plugin file truncates the run to that many plans, which is a way to
run just the first plan locally — and a trap if you did not mean to.
Commonly needed, by plugin:
all      esignet.base_url, keycloak.token_url, keycloak.client_secret
mosip    esignet.identity.individual_id, esignet.otp.ws_url,
esignet.pms.{base_url,auth_partner_id,policy_id}
sunbird  esignet.identity.individual_id, esignet.knowledge.{full_name,dob}
mock     nothing — its seed identity/login ship in config.mock.json
Optional, any plugin: api.flow_client_id — a client id already registered on
your deployment. Without it the @flow-authz-neg scenarios report
ENV_NOT_READY (reported, not failed) because they have no client to drive.
Check your overlay landed the way you expect before a long run — it prints
the merged result, runs nothing, and needs no suite:
./run-all.sh -c data/config/config.mosip.json --check
